summary: Plan created: 5 phases, 7 hours, 3 waves. Record-file prose and the Lean identifier rename run in parallel (wave 1); Lean prose and docs/typst/latex prose run in parallel (wave 2); a single full gate closes (wave 3). Exactly two full-tree lake builds are budgeted against a 241-of-479-module blast radius.

memory_candidates.content: Phase decomposition for a wide rename in a repository where the renamed symbol has a large reverse-import closure: split phases by Verification Tier so the rebuild budget is explicit and bounded. Only the interface-tier phase (the identifier/signature sweep) builds in-phase; prose-tier phases (docstrings, READMEs, external docs) declare zero in-phase build and defer their cache invalidation to the single full-tier gate phase at the end. This yields a fixed two-build budget instead of one-build-per-phase, while still isolating mechanical rename failure from prose churn -- if the interface phase's build is green and the final build is red, the fault is in prose, not in the rename. Applies whenever whole-file hashing means a comment-only edit at the base of the import graph invalidates hundreds of downstream artifacts (Lean/lake, and any build system with file-granular hashing). Pair it with Commit Mode atomic-batch on the identifier phase, since a half-renamed tree is genuinely red at every intermediate file.
